message.content:
When a new drone arrives, I add it to the fleet by setting up its details—like which model it is, what sensors it has, and which charging connector it uses—so the system knows where it belongs and how to manage it. I also make sure it’s assigned to the right home site where its charging pad is, since pads aren’t shared between companies.

When a drone is worn out, I take it out of service and retire it from the fleet. If regulators ask, I can show how it was maintained, but I don’t handle repairs myself—those are done by technicians. The drone’s data and history stay in the system until it’s fully removed, but I don’t worry about backups or long-term storage; that’s not part of my job.
